text: Make the tabernacle of ten curtains of finely twisted linen, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim worked into them by a skilled craftsman.
Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide; all the curtains are to be the same size.
Five curtains are to be joined together into one set, and the other five joined together into a second set.

versions.text: Five of the curtains are to be joined to one another, and the other five joined to one another as well.
versions.explanation: The repeated "joined to one another ... to one another as well" is clumsy when read aloud and leaves unclear that two separate sets are formed. Naming the two sets also prepares the hearer for verses 4-6, which refer to "the first set" and "the second set."

text: Make loops of blue yarn along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same along the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
Make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
Then make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle is a single whole.
Make curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle — eleven curtains in all.
Each curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide; all eleven curtains are to be the same size.
Join five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another, and fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the one set and fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the other set.
Then make fifty bronze clasps, put them through the loops, and join the tent together so that it is a single whole.
The extra length of the tent curtains — the half curtain that is left over — is to hang down over the back of the tabernacle.

versions.text: As for the overhang left over from the tent curtains, the half curtain that remains is to hang down over the back of the tabernacle.
versions.explanation: "The overhang left over ... that remains" stacks three near-synonymous words for the same idea, making the sentence heavy for oral reading. The revision keeps the sense of both סֶרַח הָעֹדֵף and הָעֹדֶפֶת while flowing more naturally.

text: The extra cubit on each side, from the length of the tent curtains, is to hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on one side and the other, to cover it.
Make for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
Make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide,
with two tenons set parallel to each other. Make all the frames of the tabernacle this way.
Make the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side,
and forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames — two bases under each frame, one for each of its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames
and forty silver bases — two under each frame.
For the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, make six frames,
and make two frames for the corners at the rear.
They are to be doubled at the bottom and joined together at the top, fitted into a single ring. Both corner frames are to be made this way.
So there will be eight frames with their silver bases — sixteen bases, two under each frame.
Make crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames at the rear of the tabernacle, on the west.
The middle crossbar, halfway up the frames, is to run from end to end.
Overlay the frames with gold, and make gold rings to hold the crossbars; overlay the crossbars with gold as well.
Set up the tabernacle according to the plan you were shown on the mountain.
Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled craftsman.

versions.text: Make a curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled craftsman.
versions.explanation: The chapter uses "curtains" throughout for the יְרִיעֹת of the tabernacle covering; rendering פָרֹכֶת with the same word blurs the distinction between the roof curtains and the inner dividing screen, which is confusing when heard. "Veil" (used consistently in verses 31, 33, and 35) keeps the two items clearly separate for a listener.

text: Hang it on four posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with gold hooks, standing on four silver bases.
Hang the curtain beneath the clasps, and bring the ark of the testimony in there, behind the curtain. The curtain will separate for you the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
Place the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony in the Most Holy Place.
Set the table outside the curtain, and the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle; put the table on the north side.
For the entrance to the tent make a screen of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
Make five posts of acacia wood for the screen and overlay them with gold, with gold hooks, and cast five bronze bases for them.
